organic.title: Organic waste
steps: Put it in the wet or green waste bin.
Compost it at home or in a community compost pit if you can.
Drain extra liquid before binning.
dont: Don't mix it with plastic, glass or paper.
Don't wrap it in a plastic bag before binning.
organic.why: Food and plant waste rots into compost. In a landfill it makes methane, a greenhouse gas.
organic.tip: Banana, orange and mango peels and egg shells are good for compost. Cooked food and meat need a proper compost system.

plastic_bottle_container.title: Plastic bottle or container
steps: Empty it and rinse it quickly.
Crush it to save space.
Keep it dry and put it in the dry waste bin, or give it to your kabadiwala or collector.
Check the number in the triangle on the bottom for specific advice.
dont: Don't recycle bottles that held pesticide, paint or chemicals. Treat them as hazardous.
plastic_bottle_container.why: Most bottles are PET (1) or HDPE (2), and both can be recycled into new products.
plastic_bottle_container.tip: The cap and the label are often different plastics. Ask your local collector whether to leave the cap on.

plastic_film.title: Plastic film and packets
steps: Empty it and shake out any food.
Keep it dry, and give it to your collector with the dry waste.
Collect packets in one bag so they don't fly away.
dont: Don't throw it in drains or open areas.
plastic_film.why: Thin plastic is hard to recycle, and many collectors take it only if it is clean and dry.
plastic_film.tip: Using fewer carry bags and packets matters more than recycling them. Check with your local collector, since acceptance varies.

paper_cardboard.title: Paper and cardboard
steps: Keep it dry and clean.
Flatten boxes.
Give it to your kabadiwala or put it in the dry waste bin.
dont: Don't recycle paper that is wet or covered in food or grease.
Don't mix it with wet waste.
paper_cardboard.why: Clean paper and cardboard can be pulped and made into new paper many times.
paper_cardboard.tip: Remove tape and staples if you can. Greasy pizza boxes can go with the wet waste.

glass.title: Glass
steps: Rinse it and take off the lids.
Put it in the dry waste or give it to your collector.
Wrap broken glass in newspaper and mark it before handing it over.
dont: Don't put broken glass loose in the bin. It can hurt waste workers.
Don't mix window glass, mirrors or bulbs with bottles and jars.
glass.why: Glass bottles and jars can be recycled again and again without losing quality.
glass.tip: Bottles and jars can often be reused at home before you recycle them.

metal.title: Metal
steps: Empty it and rinse it.
Put it in the dry waste or give it to your kabadiwala.
Crush cans to save space.
dont: Don't recycle aerosol cans that still have contents. See the hazardous advice.
Don't put sharp edges loose in the bin.
metal.why: Metals like steel and aluminium recycle well and save a lot of energy compared to making new metal.
metal.tip: Scrap metal has resale value, so collectors usually take it.

ewaste.title: Electronic waste
steps: Don't put it in the normal bin.
Take it to an authorised e-waste collection point, or to a store or brand take-back programme.
Remove personal data from phones, laptops and drives first.
dont: Don't break open or burn electronics.
Don't hand it to unauthorised scrap dealers who burn parts for metals.
ewaste.why: Electronics contain useful metals and also toxic materials such as lead and mercury.
ewaste.tip: Check with the shop where you bought it. Many brands take old devices back.
ewaste.warning: Batteries can leak or catch fire. Don't crush or burn them, and tape the ends of lithium cells.

hazardous.title: Hazardous waste
steps: Keep it separate from the other waste.
Keep it in a closed container, away from children and pets.
Take it to an authorised hazardous waste or collection point, or ask your municipality.
For medicines, ask a pharmacy or a hospital.
dont: Don't pour chemicals or medicines down the drain or on the ground.
hazardous.why: These items can poison people, animals and water, or can injure waste workers.
hazardous.tip: Broken thermometers, tube lights and CFL bulbs contain mercury. Don't touch the contents. Ventilate the room and use gloves.

unsure.title: Not sure
steps: Take another photo in good light with the item in the middle of the frame.
Or pick the type yourself from the list.
If you still don't know, ask your local waste collector.
dont: Don't guess for chemicals, batteries or medicines. Treat them as hazardous.
unsure.why: The app is only confident about the kinds of waste it was trained on.
unsure.tip: When in doubt, keep it out of the regular bin and ask.

1.name: PET
1.note: Water and cold drink bottles. Widely recycled.

2.name: HDPE
2.note: Shampoo, detergent and milk bottles. Widely recycled.

3.name: PVC
3.note: Pipes and some packaging. Hard to recycle. Ask your collector.

4.name: LDPE
4.note: Bags and films. Accepted in some places only.

5.name: PP
5.note: Tubs, lunch boxes and caps. Often recycled.

6.name: PS
6.note: Thermocol and disposable cups. Rarely recycled.
